title
Manual treadmill prototype. A three-dimensional build sequence, from reclaimed steel to a running machine.
blueprint

The design starts from two engineering drawings. The side elevation sets a fifteen-hundred-millimetre base and a twelve-hundred-millimetre running length. The front elevation fixes the frame width and a handrail height of about one thousand and fifty millimetres.
materials

Every major material is recovered. Reclaimed mild-steel square tube, forty by forty and twenty-five by twenty-five. Waste conveyor-belt rubber. An MDF deck board. Steel pipe for the rollers, pillow-block bearings, and a bag of M8 bolts, nuts and washers.
measure
Step one. Measure and mark. The base rails are marked at fifteen hundred millimetres, the cross members at five hundred, and the uprights at nine hundred and forty.
cut
Step two. Cut to length. An angle grinder with a thin cutting disc parts the tube square to the mark.
deburr
Step three. Grind and deburr. A flap disc removes the burrs and sharp edges from every cut end, so that the joints seat flat and the parts are safe to handle.
rust
Step four. Remove the rust. A wire-brush wheel strips rust and mill scale, taking the reclaimed steel from corroded brown back to bright metal.
drill
Step five. Drill the bolt holes. Eight-and-a-half-millimetre clearance holes are drilled at every joint for M8 bolts. No welding is used anywhere on the frame.
kit
The cut, cleaned and drilled kit is now ready for surface treatment.
degrease
Step six. Degrease. A solvent wipe removes oil and dust, because paint adhesion depends on a clean surface.
primer
Step seven. Prime. A rust-inhibiting primer protects the bare steel from renewed corrosion.
paint
Step eight. Paint. An industrial blue top coat is applied over the primer.
cure
Step nine. Dry and cure. The coating is left to cure fully before the parts are handled and assembled.
base

Step ten. Assemble the base frame. The two fifteen-hundred-millimetre rails sit on the front and rear cross members. Each joint takes an M8 bolt, two washers and a nut, tightened with a thirteen-millimetre spanner. Every joint is bolted, so the frame can be taken apart again. This is design for disassembly.
rollers

Step eleven. Install the rollers. Pillow-block bearings are bolted to the rails at each end, and the front and rear rollers are lowered into them. A flick of the hand confirms that each roller spins freely.
deck
Step twelve. Fit the deck. Two steel bearers are bolted along the rails, and the eighteen-millimetre MDF deck is laid on top, level with the top of the rollers.
belt

Step thirteen. Fit the belt. A continuous loop of waste conveyor belt is wrapped around the front roller, over the deck and around the rear roller, then tensioned so that it runs flat without slipping.
uprights

Step fourteen. Raise the uprights. Two twenty-five-millimetre posts are bolted to steel bracket plates at the front of the frame. The handrail is bolted across the top, and the display console is fitted at the centre.
inspect
Step fifteen. Inspect. Every bolted joint, bearing and running surface is checked before the first run.
labels
Step sixteen. Final markings. The project identification is applied to the frame.
run1
The treadmill in operation. It needs no electricity. The user's own stride drives the belt.
run2
The rubber belt slides over the MDF deck, and turns the front and rear rollers on their sealed bearings.
run3
Every joint in the frame is bolted, so any part can be removed, repaired or replaced.
run4
Built from reclaimed steel and waste conveyor belt, for a total material cost of two hundred and ninety-nine dollars and twenty-five cents, with a rated user mass of one hundred and twenty kilograms.
end
Manual treadmill prototype. Chinhoyi University of Technology, Department of Materials Science and Engineering.
